topic.title: The do-while Loop
topic.description: Loop that executes at least once

sections.title: What You'll Learn
sections.content:
Ready to learn **The do-while Loop**?

Here's what we'll cover:

• Loop that executes at least once
• Why this matters for your coding journey
• Hands-on examples you can try

sections.title: Core Concepts
sections.content:
Think of **The do-while Loop** like building blocks. 

Every great program starts with small, simple pieces. This is one of those essential pieces!

• Start simple, then build up
• Practice makes it click
• Don't worry if it takes time - totally normal!

sections.title: Code Examples
Key Points
points: The do-while loop executes the body first, then checks the condition
The body is guaranteed to execute at least once regardless of the condition
The syntax is: do { body } while (condition);
Use do-while when you need user input validation that must run at least once
The semicolon after the closing parenthesis of while is required

sections.title: Summary
sections.content: The do-while Loop - Loop that executes at least once. Master basics before advancing. Practice with the examples. Builds foundation for what's next.

questions.question: How does a do-while loop differ from a while loop?
options: It always executes the loop body at least once
It does not need a condition
It can only run a fixed number of times
questions.explanation: A do-while loop checks its condition after executing the loop body, guaranteeing that the body executes at least once, unlike a while loop which checks the condition first.

questions.question: Where is the condition checked in a do-while loop?
options: In the middle of the loop body
questions.explanation: In a do-while loop, the condition is checked after the loop body executes. The syntax is: do { statements; } while (condition);
